cues.caption: Welcome back, champ!
cues.text: Hey champ, welcome back! It's so good to see you.

cues.caption: Unit 3 · Building With Blocks · done!
cues.text: Last time, you built your very first program. You planned it, tested it, and fixed the bugs. And that finished all of Unit three. Amazing work!

cues.caption: Unit 4 · Computers in Our World
cues.text: Today, we're starting a brand new unit. Unit four. It's called, Computers in Our World. Welcome aboard!

cues.caption: Chapter 1 · Jobs That Use Computers
cues.text: And chapter one is all about, Jobs That Use Computers.

cues.caption: Who makes your games and cartoons?
cues.text: Have you ever wondered who makes the games you play, or the cartoons you watch? Let's find out!

cues.caption: Meet Meera. She loves drawing & stories
cues.text: Meet Meera. She's nine years old, and she loves drawing, and making up stories.

cues.caption: Game · Cartoon · Phone payment · Maps
cues.text: On Sunday, Meera plays a game on the tablet. Then she watches her favourite cartoon. At the chai stall, Papa pays by scanning a code on his phone. And they use a maps app, to find the new park.

cues.caption: Who made all of these? Think!
cues.text: So here's a question. Who made all of these things? Think about it.

cues.caption: Real people, using computers at work!
cues.text: Real people did! People who use computers in their jobs. And today, you'll meet four of them.

cues.caption: Game dev · App dev · Animator · Robots
cues.text: Lots of people use computers to do their jobs. Today's four are, a game developer, an app developer, an animator, and a robotics engineer.

cues.caption: Developer = someone who builds with computers
cues.text: Developer is just a big word for a builder. Someone who builds things, using a computer. Like games, or apps.

cues.caption: Game developer: levels · characters · rules
cues.text: First up, the game developer. A game developer builds video games. The levels, the characters, and the rules. They decide how high the hero can jump, and what happens when you grab a coin.

cues.caption: "if touching coin then change score by 1"
cues.text: In a coin game, a game developer might tell the computer, if touching coin, then change score by one.

cues.caption: An if-block + a variable. You know these!
cues.text: Wait a minute! That's an if block, which makes a choice. And score is a variable, a box that holds a number. You learned both of those in Unit three!

cues.caption: App developer: apps for phones & tablets
cues.text: Next, the app developer. An app developer builds apps for phones and tablets. Every little app on a phone was built by people, one step at a time.

cues.caption: Maps app: built by app developers
cues.text: Remember the maps app that found the park? App developers and engineers built that. You type where you want to go, and it shows you the way.

cues.caption: UPI payment app: one scan to pay
cues.text: And the app Papa used at the chai stall? That's a U P I payment app. App developers built it too, so paying takes just one scan!

cues.caption: Animator: makes cartoons on computers
cues.text: Then there's the animator. An animator uses computers to make cartoons, and moving pictures. Think of your favourite cartoon. Every jump, and every smile, was made by an animator.

cues.caption: Move a little, again and again → motion!
cues.text: How do cartoons move? The animator tells the computer, move the character a little, again and again. Each picture is a tiny bit different. Play them fast, and it looks like magic!

cues.caption: Meera loves drawing. Which job suits her?
cues.text: Now, remember Meera, who loves drawing and stories? Which job might suit her best? Think!

cues.caption: Animator! Drawing + stories = cartoons
cues.text: An animator! Drawing, plus stories, plus a computer, makes cartoons.

cues.caption: Robotics engineer: builds robots
cues.text: And last, the robotics engineer. A robotics engineer builds robots, and writes the steps that tell them what to do.

cues.caption: Pick up box → Turn → Put down box
cues.text: For a robot in a big warehouse, the steps might be, pick up the box. Turn around. Put down the box.

cues.caption: Robots follow algorithms people write
cues.text: Step by step instructions. Sound familiar? It's an algorithm! Robots can't guess, just like Robo in Unit two. They follow the algorithms that people write.

cues.caption: You already know their tools!
cues.text: Here's the coolest part. You already know the tools these people use!

cues.caption: Algorithms · Blocks · Variables · If-blocks
cues.text: Algorithms, step by step instructions, from Unit two. Blocks, variables, and if blocks, from Unit three. Real developers use these same ideas, every single day. So when you snapped blocks together, you were working just like them!

cues.caption: Match each job to what it tells a computer
cues.text: Let's play, match it! Three jobs, and three things they might tell a computer. Which goes with which? Pause, and match them.

cues.caption: Animator · Game developer · Robotics engineer
cues.text: Move the character a little each frame? That's the animator. Touching a coin adds to the score? The game developer. Pick up the box and turn? The robotics engineer. Great matching!

cues.caption: Nobody is born knowing how to code
cues.text: Now, you might think, these jobs are only for geniuses. But here's a secret. Nobody is born knowing how to code.

cues.caption: Like cricket: practise a little, often
cues.text: Coding is like cricket. The first time you held a bat, you probably missed the ball! But you practised a little, often, and you got better and better.

cues.caption: True or false: only adults can code?
cues.text: So, true or false? Only adults can learn to code. Hmm. What do you think?

cues.caption: False! Kids can code. You already do!
cues.text: False! Kids can code too. You've been coding all through Unit three. You're already a coder, champ!

cues.caption: Your turn: practice check
cues.text: Okay champ, it's practice check time, just like the quiz.

cues.caption: Name a job + one thing it tells a computer
cues.text: Name one job that uses computers, and one thing that person might tell a computer to do. You can pause, and try it on paper.

cues.caption: Game dev: touch a coin → add 1 to score
cues.text: Here's one answer. A game developer might tell the computer, if the player touches a coin, add one to the score. Did you pick a different job? Wonderful!

cues.caption: People use computers to make games & apps
cues.text: Let's remember. Games, apps, cartoons, and robots are made by people using computers.

cues.caption: Developers use algorithms & blocks
cues.text: Developers use algorithms and blocks, just like you!

cues.caption: No genius needed: practise often
cues.text: You don't need to be a genius. Practise a little, often.

cues.caption: Kids can code, not only adults!
cues.text: And kids can learn to code too, not only adults.

cues.caption: Chapter 1 done!
cues.text: Chapter one of Unit four, done! Welcome to Computers in Our World, champ.

cues.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
cues.text: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
